audit.summary: Confirmed major: 1 Confirmed minor: 8 Core result refuted: False
limitations: P1 — Finite-volume saturation invalidates the central cost lemmas — Counterevidence: The fixed triangle is not an infinite family and does not refute Theorem1.1. A local limit that is finite is eventually the same connected regular graph once a sufficiently large ball matches.

P2 — Closed-ball overlap invalidates a deterministic packing implication — Counterevidence: This does not refute the final probability bound. A maximal net of mutual distance>2 floor(r) has disjoint closed balls and a2R cover; its H is connected with edge lengths<=4R+1<=5R.

P3 — Variance bound needs an integer threshold or ceiling — Counterevidence: For integer thresholds the argument is not refuted. If an implicit integer convention was intended, the explicit real application still needs rounding.

P4 — Corollary2.3 is invoked with lambda below1 — Counterevidence: The retained2025 reference's finite exploration lemma applies to the entire finite graph: conditional unseen-edge law remains product, transitivity bounds the pivotal ghost event, and Bayes gives the displayed comparison without an infinite-volume limit.
P5 — The chosen radius does not control the displayed error — Counterevidence: Half the logarithmic radius, rounded down, still diverges and using r<=d^r bounds the error by delta^2/(2d).
P6 — Unrestricted eta makes a probability lower bound exceed1 — Counterevidence: The small-sprinkling range actually used admits the stated proof after restriction.

P7 — The gamma expression is not real on permitted cycles — Counterevidence: The actual Section6 use has gamma>exp((log diam)^(1/9)), eventually large. Merely flooring gamma at3 is not a proof of a new bound.

P8 — Uniformly bounded individual cycles cannot approximate a bi-infinite geodesic — Counterevidence: Growing rectangle boundaries converge pointwise to the axis and are finite sums of unit plaquettes, but have unbounded diameter. The p.45 cutset argument uses this finite-sum type of algebra, not the false sentence.

P9 — Density quantiles do not exist for certain events — Counterevidence: Generalized infimum gives zero; the ratio0/0 must also be addressed. Large-volume proof uses densities above the microscopic regime.
Limitations: The explicit triangle witnesses refute Lemmas3.5 and3.6, not the infinite-family Theorem1.1.
Limitations: The piecewise zero-cost repair was checked in the saturated branch and compactness interface; no whole-paper acceptance or author adoption is asserted.

Limitations: The radius example is an exact algebraic calculation, not an asserted graph satisfying the contradiction case of Proposition2.9.

repair.content:
Set cost to0 when floor(n^(1/3))>diamG, retaining the original cost otherwise; orange already implies green there. Finite-limit costs then vanish, while fixed-scale infinite local limits are unchanged. Propagate the altered definition and address P7 explicitly.

Use a maximal net with separation>2 floor(r). Closed balls are disjoint; 2R-cover and H-edges<=5R preserve the volume/Harris argument.

State n integer or replace n^2 by ceil(n)^2 and round the application, absorbing the bounded error.

Apply Lemma2.2 directly with h=r^-1 log(1/(1-epsilon/4)), yielding mu<=epsilon/2 and a uniform exponential bound for every n>=1.

Use half the logarithmic radius, rounded down, and r<=d^r; then error<=delta^2/(2d). New radius still diverges.

Restrict eta to the proved small range or cap the asserted bound by a fixed small-sprinkling value.

State an adequate large-gamma domain including the starting scale, or prove a separate small-gamma conclusion. Also reduce epsilon below1/2 before choosing positive alpha.

Use finite sums of bounded generators. Growing rectangle boundaries provide the correct pointwise approximation in Z2.

Use generalized infimum quantiles in[0,1] and multiplicative sharp-density inequality, or restrict alpha>1/|V|.
